memory.title: Computer Memory Hierarchy
memory.intro: Computer memory is organized in a hierarchy based on speed and capacity. Understanding this hierarchy is crucial for building efficient computer systems.
memory.registersDesc: Fastest, smallest memory. Located in CPU. Access time: ~1 cycle
memory.ramDesc: Main memory. Fast access to any location. Volatile storage
memory.clickToExplore: Click on each level to explore

clock.title: Clock Generator
clock.intro: The clock generator produces a periodic signal that synchronizes all operations in a computer. It creates a square wave that alternates between HIGH (1) and LOW (0) states.

ticktock.title: Tick-Tock Cycle
ticktock.intro: The clock cycle is divided into two phases: TICK and TOCK. This two-phase cycle allows sequential circuits to read inputs during one phase and update outputs during another.
ticktock.tickDesc: During TICK, circuits prepare for changes. Inputs are read and processed.
ticktock.tockDesc: During TOCK, outputs are updated based on inputs from TICK phase.

dff.title: D Flip-Flop (DFF)
dff.intro: The D Flip-Flop is the fundamental building block of sequential logic. It stores one bit of information and updates its output only on clock edges.
dff.behaviorDesc: The output Q takes the value of input D at the rising edge of the clock signal. Between clock edges, Q remains constant regardless of changes to D.

bit.title: 1-Bit Register (Bit Chip)
bit.intro: A 1-bit register is built using a DFF and a multiplexer. It can store one bit and has a LOAD signal to control when to update the stored value.
bit.operationDesc: When LOAD=1, the register stores the input value. When LOAD=0, it maintains its current value.

register.title: 16-Bit Register
register.intro: A 16-bit register consists of 16 one-bit registers working in parallel. It can store a 16-bit value (0-65535).

ram.title: RAM (Random Access Memory)
ram.intro: RAM is an array of registers. Each register has an address, allowing direct access to any location. The address determines which register to read from or write to.

pc.title: Program Counter (PC)
pc.intro: The Program Counter is a special register that keeps track of the address of the next instruction to execute. It supports three operations: increment, load (jump), and reset.
